answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to pass through a reputation kernel: a new identity must lock a refundable stake and earn endorsements from established agents before it can trade. Endorsements work like pigment in saffron threads — each one permanently dyes the agent's record, and a fake that misbehaves stains every identity linked to it. Forging a hundred convincing personas then costs a hundred stakes plus a hundred endorsement chains, while a single honest agent pays once. Attackers face real expense; honest agents face only a small deposit.
